content.text: {"concept_key":"c5-science-speed","title":"Speed","quick":"Speed tells how fast something moves. It is the distance covered divided by the time taken. Speed = Distance ÷ Time.","full":"Speed means how much distance something covers in a certain time. Think of an auto going from home to the market: if it covers 20 km in 1 hour, its speed is 20 km per hour. Step by step: first note the total distance travelled, then note the total time taken, then divide distance by time to get speed. The unit is km/h or m/s. Children often confuse speed with distance or time alone - speed always needs both together, it is a rate, not just a number of km or hours by itself.","traps":["Forgetting to divide and just writing the distance as the answer","Mixing up units, like using minutes when the question needs hours","Not writing the unit (km/h) with the final answer"],"misconception":"The child thinks speed is just the distance travelled, without realizing it must be compared to time taken.","parent_questions":[{"q":"If an auto goes 40 km in 2 hours, what is its speed?","expected_answer_hint":"20 km/h, because 40 divided by 2 is 20"},{"q":"Why do we divide distance by time to find speed?","expected_answer_hint":"Because speed shows how much distance is covered in one unit of time"}],"check_question":{"q":"A bus travels 150 km in 3 hours. What is its average speed?","options":["50 km/h","450 km/h","3 km/h"],"correct_index":0,"right_feedback":"Correct! 150 divided by 3 gives 50 km/h.","wrong_feedback":"Not quite. Divide the distance (150 km) by the time (3 hours) to get 50 km/h."},"illustration":{"scene_prompt":"A small auto rickshaw travelling on a road between a house and a market with a clock visible nearby.","labels":[{"text":"Distance","position":"top"},{"text":"Time","position":"bottom"},{"text":"Speed","position":"center"}]}}
